official.description: Modul University Vienna in Austria runs a family of merit scholarships for incoming international students at both undergraduate and graduate level. All of them are tuition discounts: awards are calculated as a percentage of the tuition fee from the applicant's admission-performance score, with the Graduate Excellence Scholarship capped at 25 percent for master's programmes and 50 percent for the MBA, and the Undergraduate Supporting Futures Scholarship capped at 25 percent. The only fixed euro figure published by the university is the EUR 2,000 Early Bird Reduction for early submissions.

applicant_utility.summary: Every Modul award is a tuition discount, so treat your application as a pricing question rather than a funding competition: the higher your admission-performance score, the larger the percentage you receive, with 15 percent available for scores above 90 percent and the master's total capped at 25 percent. If you have a GMAT, note the separate merit bonus, which stacks up to another 15 percent for a score of 675 or above. The one hard euro figure you can plan around with certainty is the EUR 2,000 Early Bird Reduction, which is worth more than a single small percentage band, so it is usually worth submitting a complete application by 15 March for the autumn intake even if the rest of your file is not yet perfect.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants with strong grades applying to a master's or MBA at Modul who can also submit early and who can cover the remaining tuition plus Vienna living costs themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Work out which percentage band your admission-performance score puts you in before choosing the award you request
Submit by 15 March for the Fall semester or 15 August for the Spring semester to secure the EUR 2,000 Early Bird Reduction
Check the separate Tuition Fees page for the actual fee you will be reducing, since the awards are all relative amounts
Prepare a GMAT if your grades are near a band boundary and the score lifts you into the next one
Confirm the language and admission requirements on your programme's own page, since the scholarship pages do not state them
Budget the uncovered share of tuition plus rent, food and insurance in Vienna, because no living allowance is offered
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the scholarship pays anything towards living costs, when the Graduate Excellence Scholarship covers tuition fees only
Missing the Early Bird deadlines and losing the larger EUR 2,000 reduction over a few days
Being just below a performance band and not submitting the GMAT or grade evidence that would lift the band
Confusing the MBA cap of 50 percent with the master's cap of 25 percent
Submitting a late or unmotivated application, when the university awards on a motivated and outstanding file
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: rent, food, local transport and insurance in Vienna, plus the share of tuition left after a 25 percent cap (or 50 percent for the MBA) reduction.
document_audit: Academic records must clearly show the grade percentage or GPA the award bands are based on
Keep the proof of the Early Bird submission date, since the reduction depends on it
If you claim the undergraduate SAT route, have the official score report ready as the scholarship page quotes specific SAT bands
alerts: Fees are reduced rather than replaced, so the money is paid by reducing what you owe, not by transfer to your account
The university describes its scholarship offer as expanded in 2025, so check current bands before relying on older brochure figures
Applications for the named scholarships are accepted throughout the year, so an early autumn submission does not put you at a disadvantage
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to your programme with your academic file, be assessed on admission performance, and either secure the Early Bird Reduction by the March or August deadline or receive a percentage band award applied against your tuition.
